story_type: mine-clearing line charges blast a road full of IEDs
hook: Every blast here was on purpose. The road was full of hidden bombs.
narration: Every one of these blasts was on purpose, to clear a road laced with hidden bombs.
Kajaki, Afghanistan, October 2011. Route 611 ran through a town full of improvised explosive devices.
People who lived there had been forced to leave their homes because of them.
So Marine combat engineers loaded their breaching vehicles with mine-clearing line charges.
A line charge is a rocket that drags a hundred meter hose of explosive across the ground, then sets off the bombs buried along that lane.
From above, the camera watched a rocket arc out over the fields.
[short pause] Then the whole lane went up at once.
outcome: The Marines detonated their line charges and blasted a path through the IEDs along Route 611.
title: Line charges blast a bomb-laced road
description:
In October 2011, Marines with Engineer Support Company, 3rd Combat Engineer Battalion, supporting 1st Battalion, 6th Marine Regiment, used mine-clearing line charges to clear improvised explosive devices near Route 611 in Kajaki, Afghanistan.

Footage: U.S. Marine Corps video by Cpl. Bryan Nygaard and Cpl. John M. McCall, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/128799/operation-eastern-storm-marines-make-big-bang-clearing-ieds
